item.text:
**8B.5 Research Note: Félix Tshisekedi in 2024**

**Working read:** mixed, but leaning negative on overall discipline/control. There is real evidence of coordination in civilian finance and some oversight/reform machinery, but the security apparatus, cabinet formation, and parts of the broader state still looked fragmented, proxy-heavy, and only partly under control.

| Polarity | Claim-level item | Publisher / date | Recoverable page URL | Short claim-level summary | Question IDs |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Positive | Tshisekedi finally formed a government after months of coalition delay | Reuters, 2024-05-29 | https://www.citizen.digital/article/dr-congo-names-new-government-after-months-of-delay-n343003 | Reuters reported that the cabinet impasse ended only after prolonged bargaining, with Suminwa as PM and Kamerhe as speaker paving the way. This is limited but real evidence that the president could eventually assemble a governing coalition and move it into place. | 8B.5 |
| Positive | Budget and finance teams negotiated IMF programs in a coordinated way | Ministry of Budget, 2024-11-15 | https://budget.gouv.cd/ministere-du-budget-cooperation-rd-congo-fmi/ | The ministry said the new IMF deal was negotiated by the budget minister, finance minister, and central bank governor, and was meant to implement the president’s program. This is one of the clearest signs of inter-ministerial follow-through in 2024. | 8B.5 |
| Positive | IMF-backed reform machinery included civil-service and spending-chain corrections | IMF, 2024-07-15 | https://www.imf.org/en/news/articles/2024/07/03/pr24253-drc-imf-exec-board-concludes-2024-art-iv-consult-completes-6th-rev-ecf-arr | IMF said the authorities cleaned up the civil-service register with biometrics, reorganized social security coverage, and advanced treasury/expenditure-chain reforms. That indicates some capacity for administrative correction and implementation. | 8B.5 |
| Positive | Court of Accounts oversight was explicitly backed by the presidency | Présidence RDC, 2024-10-07 | https://www.presidence.cd/actualite-detail/actualite/le_chef_de_l_etat_a_assiste_a_louverture_de_la_session_extraordinaire_du_conseil_superieur_de_la_cour_des_comptes | The Court of Accounts said Tshisekedi supported the control function and anti-corruption oversight. This is executive-hosted evidence, but it still supports the claim that he was willing to activate at least one accountability institution. | 8B.5 |
| Positive | P-DDRCS was kept staffed and maintained as a stabilization apparatus | ACP, 2024-12-20 | https://acp.cd/nation/programme-de-desarmement-et-relevement-communautaire-nomination-dune-nouvelle-equipe-de-coordination-nationale/ | A new national coordination team was appointed by presidential ordinance, showing continued institutional maintenance rather than abandonment. This supports follow-through on a demobilization/stabilization instrument. | 8B.5 |
| Positive | Tshisekedi held repeated military high-command task-force meetings | Présidence RDC, 2024-07-05 | https://presidence.cd/actualite-detail/actualite/securite_a_lest_le_chef_de_letat_a_reuni_la_task_force_du_haut_commandement_militaire | The presidency said he chaired the first task-force meeting, received tactical assessments, and ordered actions to safeguard territorial integrity. This is direct evidence of command attention and structured crisis coordination. | 8B.5 |
| Positive | A second interagency security meeting followed with implementation orders | Présidence RDC, 2024-07-09 | https://presidence.cd/actualite-detail/actualite/securite_dans_lest_le_chef_de_l_etat_a_preside_la_deuxieme_reunion_de_la_task_force_du_haut_commandement_militaire | The presidency said Tshisekedi chaired another meeting with defense, security, and finance officials and ordered implementation of measures. This is stronger evidence of sustained coordination, not just one-off signaling. | 8B.5 |
| Negative | Cabinet formation was delayed by internal jostling for posts | Reuters, 2024-05-29 | https://www.marketscreener.com/news/latest/DR-Congo-names-new-government-after-months-of-delay-46846207/ | Reuters said internal bargaining delayed cabinet formation for months and the eventual government was larger than expected. This points to weak discipline and continuing patronage pressure inside the ruling coalition. | 8B.5 |
| Negative | The army remained disorganized, proxy-dependent, and poorly controlled | Reuters, 2024-07-17 | https://theprint.in/world/army-disarray-hobbles-congos-fight-with-rwanda-backed-rebels-officers-say/2160048/ | Reuters reported senior officers describing mismanagement, weak logistics, demoralized troops, and over-reliance on Wazalendo militias the army did not control. This is the strongest counterevidence against effective command-and-control in the security sector. | 8B.5 |
| Negative | Officers said the army had no control over Wazalendo proxies | Reuters, 2024-07-17 | https://theprint.in/world/army-disarray-hobbles-congos-fight-with-rwanda-backed-rebels-officers-say/2160048/ | The same Reuters piece emphasized that the government relied on poorly trained and undisciplined proxies and that control over them was weak. That is direct evidence of fragmented coercive authority. | 8B.5 |
| Negative | Armed men briefly seized part of the presidency complex during the coup attempt | Reuters, 2024-05-19 | https://www.tbsnews.net/worldbiz/africa/democratic-republic-congo-army-says-it-thwarted-attempted-coup-855206 | The attack on the presidency complex showed a serious security failure around the center of power. It does not prove full state collapse, but it is strong evidence of weak custody and incomplete control. | 8B.5 |
| Negative | The constitutional-reform push looked like elite entrenchment, not neutral institutional discipline | Reuters, 2024-10-24 | https://www.reuters.com/world/africa/congo-president-tshisekedi-draws-criticism-over-constitutional-reform-plans-2024-10-24/ | Reuters reported a commission to examine constitutional revisions that could remove term limits and open the door to a third term. That suggests the ruling apparatus was being steered toward personal survival, which cuts against disciplined institutional follow-through. | 8B.5 |
| Negative | Election finance and procurement looked opaque in a core state body | Reuters, 2024-01-15 | https://www.reuters.com/world/africa/congo-election-commission-overspent-awarded-opaque-contracts-report-2024-01-15/ | A civil-society report cited by Reuters said CENI could not account for about $400 million and used opaque procurement. That is strong evidence of weak administrative discipline and poor financial control in a major institution. | 8B.5 |

**Synthesis**

- Best positive case: Tshisekedi did maintain some real coordination in civilian economic governance, oversight, and select state programs. The IMF process, Court of Accounts backing, and repeated security task-force meetings show that parts of the presidency were capable of organizing implementation.
- Best negative case: the security system remained badly fragmented. The army’s reliance on proxies, command confusion, and the coup attempt point to weak discipline and imperfect control at the center of coercive power.
- Net: the year shows pockets of coordination, but not a consistently disciplined, well-controlled governing system across the state.

**Search gap**

- I did not find a strong independent source directly measuring internal party discipline or day-to-day follow-through across all ministries.
- Most positive evidence comes from official readouts or program documents, so it is weaker than the Reuters and human-rights counterevidence on actual dysfunction.
